subject: minor problem with lists in knitr::spin()

messages.author: 4f6f5f995ee31178
messages.subject: minor problem with lists in knitr::spin()
parts:
Hi!

When I write a list in the R script to be processed with spin(), the next #' entry is not interpreted correctely, i.e.:

#' # Section 1
#' In this section we a re going to deal with:
#' * AAAAA
# * BBBBB
# * XXXX
#' # Section 2
#' R code for this section:
P <- 1+ 2
#' # Section 3
(end of the example)

The words "Section 2" are not interpreted as a Heading, but as simple text.
I must include R code, and thus Section 3 above is interpreted as a heading.

I'm circunventing this problem by including an R comment wit "#"

#' # Section 1
#' In this section we a re going to deal with:
#' * AAAAA
# * BBBBB
# * XXXX
#
#' # Section 2
#' R code for this section:
P <- 1+ 2
#' # Section 3
(end of the example)

An example page here
https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/3180464/contourOngmap_log.html
(note the # just after "Based on stamen.R")

Not a big issue for me, just reporting in case this is an error to be corrected.

Thanks

Agus

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] minor problem with lists in knitr::spin()
parts:
I guess you need a blank line before/after section headings. It is
generally better practice writing

# Section 1

paragraph 1

than

# Section 1
paragraph 1

because some Markdown renderers will not recognize the section heading
in the latter case.

In the case of spin(), that means

#' some text here
#'
#' # Section heading
#'
#' more text


Regards,
Yihui
